name: SparkFun Qwiic Button (red LED)
description: 12 mm tactile push button with a built-in red LED, read over I2C through an ATtiny84 running SparkFun's firmware: it debounces the button, reports pressed/clicked status, keeps time-stamped press and click queues, drives an INT line and sets the LED brightness/pulsing. 3.3 V board with 2.2 kΩ I2C pull-ups. I2C address 0x6F (0x60-0x6F with the A0-A3 jumpers, or set in software). Sold as: SparkFun Qwiic Button - Red LED (BOB-15932), 5-pin 0.1" header INT, SCL, SDA, 3.3V, GND plus two Qwiic connectors.
eli5: A push button with a light inside that tells your board over two wires whether it is pressed, and lets your board turn the light on.

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output, active low, pulled up to 3.3 V by 10 kΩ on the board; goes low on press/click when enabled. Not needed for basic use

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (2.2 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (2.2 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on the board)

pins.name: 3.3V
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V (no regulator on the board; the Qwiic system is 3.3 V only)

supplierQuery: SparkFun Qwiic Button Red LED BOB-15932
buildNotes: Power it from 3.3 V only: the board has no regulator and its I2C pull-ups go to its own 3.3V pin.
Register reads: write the register number, then read; 16- and 32-bit registers are little-endian. Register 0x00 must read 0x5D.
Button status register 0x03: bit 2 = pressed now, bit 1 = has been clicked, bit 0 = new event; write 0 to clear bits 0 and 1.
LED: write 0-255 to register 0x19 (brightness) and 0 to the pulse cycle time 0x1B/0x1C for steady light.
Default address 0x6F. Closing jumpers A0-A3 pulls address bits low (address 0b0110 A3 A2 A1 A0); a software-set address is kept in EEPROM.
INT is only needed for interrupt-driven code; it is active low with a 10 kΩ pull-up on the board.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from qwiic_button import QwiicButton

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
btn = QwiicButton(i2c)
print('ID=0x%02X' % btn._read(0x00, 1)[0])
presses = 0
last = None
while True:
    p = btn.is_pressed()
    if p != last:
        if p:
            presses += 1
            btn.led_on(255)
            print('PRESSED %d' % presses)
        else:
            btn.led_off()
            print('RELEASED %d' % presses)
        last = p
    time.sleep_ms(50)
